stories.headline: S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory as Nasdaq posts worst week since 2020
stories.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39 and the Dow dropped 1.93% to 48,147.33 on Friday, both crossing the 10%-from-peak threshold that defines a correction. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.28% to 22,617.73, its second-worst day of 2026 and worst week since 2020, erasing all of its yearly gains as the S&P logged its seventh straight losing day, the longest such streak since February 2020.

stories.headline: Nvidia plunges 14%, down 47.5% from October peak, as AI trade selloff deepens
stories.summary: Nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, down 14% on the day and 47.5% below its October record high of $239.24, after seven straight sessions of losses. The decline dragged other chip and AI infrastructure names lower, with CoreWeave down nearly 80% from its 2025 peak, Oracle off about 70%, and AMD down 20.5%, as investors questioned whether massive AI capital spending will generate adequate returns.

stories.headline: Anthropic shares slide for second day after record $81 billion IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic (ANT), which priced the largest IPO on record and raised $81 billion, closed its debut day 17% above its $83 offering price before falling roughly 9-10% on its second trading day as the broader tech selloff intensified. Analyst Dan Ives argued the strong IPO demand shows underlying appetite for AI remains intact despite the panic, but the stock's reversal has become a flashpoint for concerns about AI valuations.

stories.headline: Bitcoin and crypto market slump as 'extreme fear' grips investors
stories.summary: Bitcoin ended the week near $58,895, down 9.8% for the week and more than 50% below its 2025 high, dragging total crypto market value down to about $2.01 trillion, roughly half its peak. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 9 ('extreme fear'), and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $582.2 million in net outflows on Thursday alone as the AI-driven selloff spread into digital assets.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs warns stock selloff has further room to run
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs research flagged that the current market downturn may not be over, noting the VIX volatility index is approaching elevated 'panic' levels last seen in prior sharp corrections. The VIX closed the week at 35.89, up 26.2%, underscoring investor anxiety about further downside in equities tied to AI spending concerns.

stories.headline: Nvidia falls behind Alphabet in market capitalization after $2.3 trillion value wipeout
stories.summary: Nvidia's market value has fallen enough that the chipmaker has slipped behind Alphabet in market capitalization, having shed roughly $2.3 trillion in value since its October peak. The reversal highlights a broader reassessment of AI-sector leadership as megacap tech valuations compress amid the selloff.

stories.headline: Gold and silver tumble as investors scramble for cash; Goldman sees more pain
stories.summary: Gold futures fell 4.62% as investors liquidated holdings across asset classes to raise cash amid the broader market rout, with Goldman Sachs warning of further downside. Bitcoin notably bucked the metals selloff with a modest intraday gain even as the broader crypto market remained under pressure for the week.

stories.headline: Mortgage rates surge, pushing homeownership further out of reach
stories.summary: Rising mortgage rates are squeezing housing affordability further, with the Financial Times reporting that the climb in borrowing costs is pricing more prospective buyers out of the market. The pressure compounds concerns about consumer spending power as broader financial conditions tighten amid the equity selloff.
